text:
eva: CI red on master — flaky failure in runtime/backoff_timer_test, failing nondeterministically across runners. seen 3 failures in the last hour: <https://ci.redwood.ai/build/34211|build/34211>
ci-bot: Build failed on ubuntu-22.04-x86-64 (node: runner-17) — test runtime/backoff_timer_test failed, logs attached.
matt: re-ran the job, linking here: <https://ci.redwood.ai/build/34213|rerun/34213>
ci-bot: Rerun started by matt.
alex: I grabbed the logs from 34211 — seems like a timer ordering / wakeup-race. snippet: ```
[ RUN      ] BackoffTimerTest.RestartsPreserveSchedule
runtime/backoff_timer_test.cc:87: Failure
Expected: next_wakeup == fixed_time (1000)
  Actual: 999 vs 1000
Stack: runtime::Timer::check_next_wakeup+0x58
```
shreya: ugh that's the off-by-one we saw last quarter but only in high-load CI. can you repro locally with stress runs? try `bazel test //runtime:backoff_timer_test --runs_per_test=50`
eva: I started a local run with `--runs_per_test=200` and hit it once within ~80 runs. attaching local log.
matt: can we bisect to find regressing commit? I can spare a machine for an automated bisect if we have a reproduce script.
alex: propose this bisect flow:
```
git checkout HEAD
git bisect start
git bisect bad HEAD
git bisect good v1.15.2
# run single-run test, exit nonzero on failure
bazel test //runtime:backoff_timer_test --test_arg=--runs=1 || exit 1
# or use helper: ./scripts/bisect_run_once.sh
```
shreya: I'll prepare `scripts/bisect_run_once.sh` to wrap the Bazel invocation and collect failure metadata. also add `--test_output=errors` so we capture the failing assertion.
eva: if anyone can run the bisect, please tag me. otherwise i'll queue it tomorrow morning on the bisect host. note: the failure is flaky so bisect might be noisy — recommend adding a short harness that seeds deterministic RNG and retries each commit N times before declaring "good".
alex: agrees — wrapper should run the test 3 times per commit and return failure only if any run fails. will make PR to scripts.
matt: quick question — could this be impacted by thread pool size change from the perf/worker-scheduler patch last week? that touched Timer::schedule paths.
shreya: yup that's my suspicion. I'll include toggles to revert that scheduling change during bisect to confirm. also, add `TEST_RANDOM_SEED=42` env to reduce noise.
eva: can someone run an initial bisect with the current wrapper (3 runs per commit) and ping here with progress? if it points to a commit in scheduler, we can file a targeted revert/patch.
ci-bot: FYI — flaky-detection bot flagged this test as flaky (score 0.37) and added to flaky-tests queue.
alex: started a bisect job on bisect-host-2, ETA ~2h, will post updates. command used: `./scripts/bisect_helper.sh --test //runtime:backoff_timer_test --runs 3`
matt: thanks alex. if it ends up being a race, we should add a short repro and a comment in the test referencing the root cause. also consider marking it flaky in CI until fixed.
shreya: I'll prep a tiny PR that makes the test deterministic by forcing `Timer::use_cooperative_mode_for_tests = true` behind a test-only flag, so CI runs are stable while we bisect.
eva: assign the follow-up: @shreya to open hotfix PR, @alex to finish bisect, @matt to review revert if needed. please update the flaky-tests board ticket #FT-112. :thumbsup:
alex: bisect found candidate regressor: commit 9f3b2c4 (perf/worker-scheduler) — reproducer hits failure in ~1/40 runs on that commit, good on prior. filing PR to revert the scheduling tweak and add a unit test that asserts deterministic wakeup ordering.
matt: nice. once PR is up, i'll run upstream CI with `--runs_per_test=200` to be sure.
eva: thanks team. logging this thread to the incident/triage notes. we'll follow up with postmortem if revert lands.
ci-bot: Flaky ticket updated: FT-112 -> status: investigating.
__note: Document is a single Slack thread: root message + replies in chronological order. Messages are short, slack style, include code blocks and links.
